newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities continue to slip.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities continue to slip.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options continued to erode Friday, but dealers said most of the slippage was because of weekend time-decay pressure.

"Volatilities have held pretty well even though we traded up," a Treasury bond trader at a brokerage firm said. "I think with the FOMC and employment next week" volatilities would at worst hold steady.

The Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee, which sets interest rate policy, meets next Tuesday and Wednesday. The all-important employment report for January is scheduled for release at 0730 CST/1330 GMT Friday.
"They've taken out about a quarter point in the March, but it's really just because of the weekend," the trader said, referring to implied volatilities on March T-bond futures-options.
Implied volatility for March T-bond futures options was quoted at around 10.60 percent, down from the 10.80 percent quoted Thursday afternoon.
"There was pretty good interest in selling volatility early on," a Treasuries dealer at a U.S. bank said.
"So net net volatility is off, which isn't totally surprising considering the market held again."
Debt futures rallied after the government reported fourth quarter gross domestic product grew at a solid pace but that inflation pressures remained light.
Short-covering in bonds also helped, traders said.
March T-bond futures rose 28/32 to 111-14/32 and the lead June Eurodollar futures gained five basis points to 94.28.
Traders said the options activity was largely directionless.
"Overall what we've seen is what I would describe as a mixed bag," the bank dealer said. "It hasn't been compellingly bullish or bearish.

"I think that's probably indicative of a little position unwinding," he said. "We did see some selling of puts earlier in the week and I think we might have seen a little short covering of those short put positions into the rally today."
T-bond traders said much of the activity was from position adjustments, with one of the most common strategies being call spreads.
In Eurodollar futures-options, traders said one of the biggest trades was from a U.S. bank that bought about 3,000 of the April 94.00 puts. One trader said that could have been short covering.

Traders said implied volatilities for June Eurodollar futures-options was around 11.05 percent, down from about 11.40 percent Thursday, and implied volatilities in September contracts fell to the 13.85 to 13.90 region from 14.30.
